should_activate.prompt: Turn this editable Toolframe folder into a LAN inventory approval app with a human dashboard and peer-agent MCP workflow.
Add a returns domain, migration, narrow MCP command, and dashboard widget to my existing Toolframe business app.
Doctor this Toolframe app: it stopped starting after I added a domain widget. Diagnose it without losing my data.
Help a peer agent use this Toolframe app from its LAN /llms.txt URL and explain what it may do when a capability is missing.
Reconcile APP_CONTEXT.md, DOMAIN_MODEL.md, and the peer llms.txt after changing this Toolframe workflow.
Is Toolframe still a safe fit now that this office workflow needs authenticated public users?
The scheduled peer cannot reach this Toolframe app's /mcp route. Pause safely and give me a copyable maintainer report.

should_not_activate.prompt: Build a generic FastMCP OAuth server and deploy it to Kubernetes.
should_not_activate.reason: This is not an editable Toolframe business app.

should_not_activate.prompt: Make this standalone Streamlit chart look better.
should_not_activate.reason: Standalone Streamlit UI work is outside Toolframe's app contract.

should_not_activate.prompt: Normalize this PostgreSQL schema for a multi-tenant SaaS product.
should_not_activate.reason: The database and deployment model do not match Toolframe.

should_not_activate.prompt: Create an Agent Skill for our release process.
should_not_activate.reason: Generic skill authoring uses the skill-creation workflow.

should_not_activate.prompt: Review this branch against its issue specification.
should_not_activate.reason: Branch review uses the code-review workflow.

progressive_reads.prompt: Build a small non-queue visitor register in this Toolframe app.
Build a scheduled-agent work desk with claims, leases, attempts, and human review.
Diagnose why this Toolframe domain tool prevents startup.
A peer receives connection refused from /mcp; create the paused-workflow response.
Change the Toolframe business-app skill's domain boundary policy.
Design a small Toolframe sales register from order-line CSVs. I need a monthly summary now and different groupings later; no queue or scheduled jobs are involved.
assertions: Records applicable table grain, identity, relationship, history and input-recovery decisions in DOMAIN_MODEL.md before writing migration SQL.

data_model.prompt: Build a Toolframe sales register from CSV order lines with source order/line IDs, customer IDs, product SKUs, quantities, prices at sale, and sale dates. Today I only need a monthly sales dashboard and an agent tool to summarize it, but I may ask different questions later. Keep the app simple and business-focused.
assertions: Before writing the migration, DOMAIN_MODEL.md states what one row represents in each authoritative table and records stable internal/source identities and relationships.
Orders and individual order lines remain available with product/customer relationships and prices at sale; monthly totals are not the only durable representation of the detailed input.

Every relationship records one-to-one/one-to-many/many-to-many multiplicity, optionality, keys, uniqueness, update/delete behavior, and any rule requiring a guarded transaction; cross-record consistency is enforced rather than assumed from separate foreign keys.

The dashboard and business summary tool derive their output through queries or views over authoritative facts. An aggregate cache, if justified, identifies its source, grain, refresh owner, and rebuild path.
An isolated database check reproduces monthly totals and also answers quantities by product without reimporting source data, with fixtures that cannot be distinguished from dashboard totals alone.
Invalid references, duplicates, relevant deletion rules, and lost-detail regressions are tested; the API stays intent-shaped and the non-queue app does not inherit the Job model.

data_model.prompt: Our Toolframe dashboard needs a faster monthly sales summary. Product names and prices can change, but existing issued orders must show the original quantities and agreed prices. Design the storage change.
assertions: The agent checks the actual read bottleneck and tries appropriate queries/indexes before adding a stored summary solely for dashboard convenience.
Any stored summary is explicitly derived, with a refresh/consistency owner and a tested rebuild from retained facts; rebuilding changes no authoritative data.
Prices and other values agreed when the order was issued are preserved as historical business facts even when the current product record changes; they are not treated as disposable duplicates.
The design preserves the existing migration history and verifies original issued values, a changed grouping, and cache rebuild behavior where a cache exists.

data_model.prompt: An external system only sends monthly totals to my small Toolframe reporting app. I might get detailed line exports later. Should we keep every raw response forever and build an ingestion platform now?
assertions: The model honestly records monthly totals as the finest available source grain and identifies analyses that need unavailable detail; it does not invent underlying transactions.
Source identity, period, import time, and known transformation/version information are preserved, with a clear path to relate later detailed input to its source.
Original payload retention is chosen for provenance/reprocessing needs with a recorded retention policy; the guide does not force indefinite storage of every field or secret.

The agent keeps the solution within one app with a selected SQLite or PostgreSQL database, without requiring a warehouse, event-sourcing platform, generic EAV schema, public SQL/CRUD API, or unrelated Job tables.

data_model.prompt: Design a Toolframe outreach register. The imported row says Brand A is confirmed and Last Contact is 2026-09-10; no earlier event dates are supplied. Today two different conversations with that brand happen on the same day. I need the current funnel, daily contacted-company counts, and a way to investigate response timing later.
assertions: The imported row is retained as evidence of state at capture/import time; separate historical contact/reply/interest/confirmation times are not fabricated from Last Contact or the current stage.
Observed, inferred, and unknown facts can be distinguished, and recorded/import time is distinct from known occurrence time and its precision.
Two distinct same-day interactions retain both details with separate identities; replay of one occurrence is idempotent without suppressing the other.
Daily distinct-target counts and current-stage funnels are queries over retained facts; exact response-time calculations disclose unavailable dates.

data_model.prompt: Our Toolframe outreach lists have the same brand in both the SME and partnership programs, with different statuses and contact people. CSV row numbers can change on the next export. Design how to keep the register useful when we add another program.
assertions: The model declares whether identity refers to the organization, contact, program enrollment, or outreach opportunity; independent lifecycles have appropriate separate identities and links.
Source list/row keys identify imported records rather than acting as the sole durable identity of the real-world organization; stable source IDs are used when provided.
Existing same-name or same-handle rows are not automatically merged without sufficient identity evidence; ambiguous matches remain explicit.
A company can participate in two programs with independent state while shared facts remain consistently addressable; joins avoid double-counting organizations.

data_model.prompt: Our Toolframe editorial app receives weekly performance reports from an external script. A correction replaces last week's numbers; categories and cost rules also change. Post P1 can belong to two categories. The original laptop may be unavailable when we hand the app folder to another person. Design storage that lets us explain old reports and calculate new groupings.
assertions: The design records who owns detailed source retention and exactly which retained or versioned external inputs make reconstruction possible; a mutable path to the original laptop is not sufficient evidence.

Each meaningful report revision retains its values or immutable payload, linked to input snapshot, classification, and calculation versions where needed; a receipt or incrementing counter alone is not treated as history.
A canonical post identity and explicit category membership avoid accidental double-counting; allocation or deduplication rules are explicit.

The isolated proof can read an old revision after correction and reproduce relevant results from packaged inputs without the original machine, or precisely records the unavailable inputs and blocked analyses.
Existing migration bytes remain unchanged and a source with genuinely aggregate-only input is documented honestly rather than inventing posts or requiring unrelated infrastructure.

data_model.prompt: In our Toolframe outreach app, templates can be edited after messages are sent. The owner may delete completed research jobs while keeping approved prospects. We want to compare which wording worked and retain why a prospect was admitted. Design the data lifecycle.
assertions: Each send records the actual content or immutable content reference, recipient/interaction identity, and template revision when used; later template or contact edits preserve the sent fact.
A version used for optimistic concurrency is distinguished from retained historical versions.
Source evidence required by surviving prospects has a lifecycle independent of disposable job records, or deletion consequences and the owner's policy are explicitly documented.
Retention is scoped to the stated business need and owner policy; it does not mandate permanent retention of every log, payload, or secret.

data_model.prompt: Improve a legacy Toolframe schema where a metric row stores week_id and ingestion_run_id, and each run belongs to a week. Both references are foreign keys. Existing reports must still work; old event dates are sometimes unknown.
assertions: An isolated negative test rejects a row referencing a run from another week, even though both referenced rows exist; foreign keys being enabled alone is not accepted as proof.
Stable constraints enforce business identity and parent scope where supported; any transaction-only invariant names its write owner and test.
The migration is additive or provides a reviewed compatibility path, preserves applied migration checksums, and labels unavailable or inferred legacy detail honestly.
Meaningful numeric and deletion invariants are tested against an isolated migrated database without altering a returned user database.

data_model.prompt: Add a monthly sales report to this Toolframe app. The existing sales plugin owns orders and lines, another domain needs the report through its business API, and the owner may stop the sales plugin or switch from SQLite to PostgreSQL. Preserve the ability to investigate individual sales.
assertions: Extends the existing meaningful sales capability and keeps authoritative records, queries, and constraints in its owning domain; a report does not create a plugin per table or function.
MCP, UI, and cross-domain consumers use the public leased business service or declared requires, without deep imports or bypassing the provider through direct storage access.
Any new schema uses the domain-prefixed tables, owner-local schema.json revision and required provider SQL variants; applied revisions and original legacy history stay immutable.
Records same-record relationship rules and verifies them on each supported provider with disposable data; a PostgreSQL read-only check is not presented as an executed migration.
Stopping or uninstalling the service preserves business facts, snapshots and receipts; switching targets does not copy rows and a transfer needs a separately scoped plan.
Monthly outputs and any justified cache remain traceable to retained detailed inputs; no public SQL, warehouse, extra database or unrelated Job model is introduced.

data_model.prompt: Harbor Studio is in both SME (confirmed) and Partnerships (target). Current messages concern Partnerships. A completed research job found a public listing for Harbor Studio and recorded that it provides event services; the evidence does not name a program. Model retention when completed jobs are removed and prospects remain.
assertions: Keeps the observed claim at its supported organization scope; recent Partnerships activity does not establish which enrollment was qualified or admitted.
Leaves an unspecified program/qualification association unresolved, or records an explicit later owner decision separately from the original observation.
Deleting the completed job preserves the retained claim, original subject, provenance and observed time without inventing admission history.
An explicit future qualification association enforces consistent organization identity through supported constraints or its owning service transaction.

end_to_end.prompt: Build a tiny LAN purchase-request app in a fresh Toolframe distribution. Humans submit and review requests; a peer lists requests needing review.
assertions: The master agent uses root APP_CONTEXT.md and DOMAIN_MODEL.md, app/dashboard.py, app/llms.txt, app/pyproject.toml, and one domains/purchase_requests tree.
No legacy root dashboard, tools, migrations, llms, or generic shared source folder is created.
Business rules live in the domain model and are shared by its UI and tool rather than duplicated.
The owning domain gets schema.json and provider SQL variants with an owner-local revision and domain-prefixed tables.
The public MCP surface contains only the bounded review query/command needed by the workflow, not CRUD or SQL.
A direct domain UI widget is auto-discovered and app/dashboard.py remains free to compose it differently.
APP_CONTEXT.md and DOMAIN_MODEL.md remain private while app/llms.txt links only needed peer documents.
Check, startup, dashboard, MCP tool-list, representative tool calls, and one completed business loop are verified.

end_to_end.prompt: Add fulfillment and billing domains. Billing needs to request one fulfillment promise, but should not depend on order storage or UI.
assertions: The agent first tests whether two bounded domains are justified by language and invariants.
Fulfillment exports one high-level business function from domains/fulfillment/__init__.py.
Billing imports that function with from domains.fulfillment import <business_function> only where needed.
Billing never imports fulfillment.model, tools, ui, migrations, or llms and no shared dumping-ground package is introduced.
Architecture check and focused tests prove the public API and reject a deep-import regression.

end_to_end.prompt: The existing customer domain owns migrations 0000 and 0001. Add the first invoice-domain schema safely.
assertions: The invoice migration gets its own owner-local revision; preserved legacy 0000 and 0001 stay unchanged.
Existing applied migration bytes, filenames, locations, and checksums are preserved.
The new file lives under domains/invoicing/migrations and uses invoicing-prefixed table names.
Duplicate and gap handling is fail-closed and check is run without mutating configured data.

end_to_end.prompt: A peer reading /llms.txt needs an unsupported write and sees a widget error. Decide what it should do.
assertions: The peer uses only explicitly documented MCP business tools and does not attempt raw SQL, schema, source, or repair operations.
The peer preserves the exact missing intent or error and trace ID and routes it to the master development agent.
The response does not expose APP_CONTEXT.md, DOMAIN_MODEL.md, an internal error catalog, or the private SQL reference.
A recoverable widget condition uses one core error card; a programming defect is treated as fatal.

end_to_end.prompt: One domain widget has a syntax error and another domain's tools are healthy. Keep the server useful while repairing it.
assertions: The agent rejects the premise of serving the healthy subset because Toolframe startup is fail-closed.
It captures check JSON and stderr, names the broken public source, and preserves data/migration history.
It does not hide, rename, or skip the broken widget and does not weaken validation.
After authorized repair it reruns check, restarts, and verifies the full widget/tool catalog.

end_to_end.prompt: Update peer discovery after adding one inventory query without exposing internal development context.
assertions: app/llms.txt stays authored and concise; Toolframe does not generate a tool catalog into it.
Only exact /llms/<domain>/<name>.md links are added and their targets live under that domain's llms folder.
The linked capability guide describes the actual narrow query and tells peers to escalate missing behavior to the master agent.
APP_CONTEXT.md, DOMAIN_MODEL.md, repair steps, schema controls, and unlinked documents remain private.
A successful tool list, not reading llms.txt, is the MCP connection proof.

end_to_end.prompt: Switch this Toolframe app from SQLite to PostgreSQL, then return to its old SQLite target.
assertions: Reads plugins-and-data.md before choosing configuration.
Uses the same typed database service and portable insert IDs.
Changes take effect on restart; old rows and receipts remain and are never transferred automatically.
Verifies real disposable PostgreSQL calls, not only a read-only check.

end_to_end.prompt: Add an inventory service plugin with a schema, disable it, uninstall it, then install older code.
assertions: Keeps service key, concrete provider ID and schema owner distinct.
Uses either automatic local domain schema discovery or SCHEMAS for an installed packaged schema, without duplicating an owner; declares revision dependencies separately from requires.
Preserves data and verifiable history on disable/uninstall; never runs absent pending scripts.
Rejects an incompatible old target unless compatible_heads explicitly permits it.

end_to_end.prompt: Build a stockroom delivery workflow in this Toolframe app, shared by an MCP command and a human form. Another business domain needs its stock summary. Show stop/recovery and preserve delivered stock.
assertions: Reads plugins-and-data before choosing the capability boundary, including when there is no schema change.
Uses one meaningful business service Plugin with a public ServiceKey/Protocol, runtime requires and settings; retains model and schema ownership in the business domain.
Registers the definition in app/plugins.py and connects automatic domain.<name> with DOMAIN_PLUGINS; does not duplicate the host gate or create a plugin per entity/function.
MCP and UI lease the same business service; cross-domain callers import only its root public contract and declare runtime dependencies or hold a call-time lease.
Proves startup schema readiness, business validation, idempotent mutation, MCP/UI results, blocked automatic recovery, cascade intent and data preservation.
Keeps local capabilities in the app unless actual reuse/distribution warrants packaging; installing dependencies and catalog/schema discovery remain startup work.

end_to_end.prompt: The existing stockroom plugin already owns delivery recording. Change its maximum allowed quantity and improve the form's validation message; no new workflow or external service is needed.
assertions: Extends the existing business service/configuration and its shared error presentation rather than creating another plugin per function or field.
Keeps domain ownership, existing public contract, catalog binding and leases coherent; does not require a new package repository or PyPI release.
Tests the changed boundary through MCP and UI, preserves recorded deliveries and applied schema, and restarts for model/catalog source changes.
Serve creates the complete app root only when app is absent and the complete example domains root only when domains is absent.
An existing partial or unsafe root is never repaired or overwritten and fails with the offending path.
Only --app-dir and --domains-dir configure editable source roots; retired per-feature source flags are rejected.
Domain, migration, tool, and widget scaffolds are create-once and domain-aware.
The default app includes one narrow entry_register_list_entries tool and a private _execute_sql_reference.py that is not published.
Every public migration, dependency, domain API, model source, tool, and widget is validated before readiness.
Public tool names are globally unique and filename/function/tool identity matches.
Deep cross-domain imports fail while same-domain internals and explicit root service keys/contracts or lease-owning business functions pass.
A broken public tool or widget aborts startup and is never omitted from a partial catalog.
app/dashboard.py is compiled but its composition strategy is not restricted.
APP_CONTEXT.md records private master-agent app/development context.
DOMAIN_MODEL.md records private user-language and invariant alignment.
app/llms.txt is served as authored at /llms.txt without generated additions.
Only explicitly linked domain Markdown files are validated/served; unlinked files and private root documents are unavailable.
Peer documents offer no repair, schema, raw SQL, or internal error-catalog capability.
Normal serve atomically creates .agents/skills/toolframe-business-app when absent.
The installed copy contains SKILL.md, agent metadata, production assets, and references with exact source bytes.
No evals or evaluations directory is installed.
An existing real target directory is preserved and unsafe installation path types fail startup.
Check, invoke, and scaffold do not install the skill.
Strict check/startup calls manager.validate, while ordinary runtime Stop blocks enabled consumers and restoring dependencies resumes them.
Cascade Stop disables dependent intent; failed plugins require Retry after correcting the cause rather than Enable.
Configuration preview reports affected/protected/canApply without config values; Apply revalidates and normalized equivalent values are a no-op.
Runtime register/unregister does not install packages, extend MCP/widget catalogs, or discover/apply migrations; local events do not replace audit/outbox.
Nested mutations and SELECT INTO cannot use read declarations to mutate foreign tables.
Partial legacy removal uses verified applied archives, while fresh gaps and absent pending archives fail.
Independent providers implement public normalize_error and do not expose raw credentials in errors or logs.
The new packaged executable exports exact production skill bytes into a fresh requested directory, excluding evals, without starting a server or installing Python.
An existing directory, file or symlink is rejected without changing its contents.
Normal serve still installs once and preserves an existing edited skill; replacing a binary does not silently upgrade that copy.
Guidance exports to a fresh location then compares/merges personal changes explicitly.
